slides.title: Dungeon Battle: Rise of Hero
slides.subtitle: Repository-grounded review of the current Java RPG architecture, implemented features, and OOP design decisions.

slides.title: A Java RPG used as both a game prototype and an OOP case study
slides.lead: The project combines a start screen, tile-based world exploration, and turn-based combat while showcasing abstraction, inheritance, interfaces, and service-driven battle rules.
bullets: Battle actors are modeled in a dedicated domain layer under entities and interfaces.
Swing-based world and battle screens provide visible progress beyond console-only exercises.
Technical documentation already maps architecture, runtime flow, UML, and OOP analysis.

slides.title: The challenge is not only making the game run, but keeping the design extensible
slides.lead: A teaching project like this must show real gameplay progress while also demonstrating why OOP matters for maintainability, reuse, and future feature growth.
bullets: Game actors need shared rules without duplicating health, damage, and defense logic.
Battle flow should remain reusable across UI layers instead of being rewritten per screen.
World exploration and battle encounters should eventually connect through a single domain model.

slides.footer: Most mature OOP implementation is concentrated in the battle domain and its services, while the scene integration layer is still evolving.

slides.title: Layer separation is good, but the main runtime path is still split
slides.lead: The repo already follows a mostly layered direction, yet the default application path still opens a separate battle prototype instead of the domain-backed battle flow.
bullets: Domain layer: Character hierarchy, enemy subclasses, and behavioral interfaces.
Service layer: BattleService, RandomEventService, and EnemyFactory orchestration.
Presentation layer: start screen, world exploration, BattleGUI, and ui.battle prototype.
Main integration gap: world encounters do not yet create real domain Enemy objects.
slides.alt: Application architecture with two runtime paths
slides.caption: Based on docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/RUNTIME_FLOW.md.

slides.title: The battle domain shows clear abstraction and reusable class relationships
slides.lead: The strongest OOP story in the repository lives inside the battle model, where shared state is abstracted and specialized behavior is pushed to subclasses and interfaces.
bullets: Character and Enemy are abstract because they represent concepts, not direct runtime instances.
Attackable captures universal combat behavior without forcing UI dependencies.
SkillUser is optional, so only Player, Goblin, and DragonBoss expose skill behavior.
Enemy subclasses override attack logic while preserving a common combat contract.

slides.caption: Grounded in docs/UML_NOTES.md and the entities/interfaces packages.

slides.title: Packages are already organized by responsibility

bullets: entities and interfaces define the combat model.
services coordinate battle flow and runtime variation.
ui.world and ui.battle show that presentation concerns are already split into scenes.

slides.title: Character centralizes state protection and attack variants
slides.lead: Encapsulation is strongest in the battle domain. HP clamping, defense state, and overloaded attack behavior are handled inside the shared abstraction rather than scattered across subclasses.
bullets: private fields guard internal combat state.
setHp(...) prevents invalid values automatically.
attack(...) overloads support extension without renaming the core action.
slides.caption: Condensed from src/fantasyrpg/entities/Character.java.

slides.title: BattleService applies polymorphism through shared contracts
slides.lead: The service does not need a special branch for every enemy class. It relies on the Enemy parent type and the optional SkillUser contract to decide how the turn resolves.
bullets: UI can pass actions at a high level without owning damage formulas.
instanceof SkillUser enables optional behavior only when the object supports it.
The returned ActionResult keeps battle logic decoupled from rendering.
slides.caption: Condensed from src/fantasyrpg/services/BattleService.java.

slides.title: Where the main OOP concepts appear in the running project
findings: Encapsulation: Character protects HP, defense, and turn modifiers through private fields and controlled methods.
Inheritance: Player and Enemy extend Character, and Enemy is specialized into Goblin, OrcWarrior, and DragonBoss.
Polymorphism: BattleService calls enemy.attack(player) and lets the concrete subclass decide the formula.
Abstraction + Interface: Character and Enemy are abstract; SkillUser adds optional skill capability without forcing every class to implement it.
Overloading + Composition: Character overloads attack(...), while BattleGUI composes BattleService and RandomEventService.

slides.title: The main issues are architectural consistency, not lack of code
findings: The default runtime path enters ui.battle.GameFrame, while the cleaner OOP battle flow lives in ui.BattleGUI.
EnemyFactory exists but is not yet the real bridge from world encounters to instantiated domain enemies.
There are two Player classes in different packages, which is valid but easy to confuse during onboarding.
Asset loading mixes direct filesystem access and classpath resource patterns, complicating packaging later.
World-side classes expose mutable state more openly than the domain layer, so encapsulation quality is uneven.

slides.title: The project already demonstrates meaningful OOP progress
slides.verdict: The strongest achievement so far is a believable battle domain with real abstraction, subtype behavior, and service-based orchestration. The next step is to unify the runtime around that stronger core.
tradeoffs: The battle domain is the clearest academic OOP success in the repository.
Playable scenes and documentation make the progress presentation concrete and defensible.
The biggest engineering task ahead is consolidation, not starting from zero.

winner.label: Recommended next focus
winner.rmse: Make BattleService the only combat source of truth
